_comment: Game map -> scrims site mapId.
Keyed on the MapRotation SHORT NAME, which DIScore derives from the
MapData asset name (DA_MapData_FragrantShore -> FragrantShore). This is the
same vocabulary TripwireServer.ini's MapRotation uses, so the server's
rotation and this table speak one language.
Why not mapCode: it does not separate the variants. LVL_FragrantShore
(confirmed Day) reports mapCode 'fs', which the Night variant shares, so
keying on the code would silently file Night matches as Day.
NOTE the asymmetric naming, from docs/01-server-config.md: Hardsell is the
NIGHT map with an explicit Hardsell_Day variant, while FragrantShore is the
DAY map with an explicit FragrantShore_Night variant. The user confirmed
LVL_FragrantShore = Fragrant Shore (Day), which corroborates it.
Resolution order is map_short_name, then map_file_name, then map_code, then
the level name - so the older file-name keys still work for a report
produced before the short name existed.
The mapId values were originally transcribed from a screenshot of the
site's table - 32-character random strings, where one misread character
would silently target the wrong map. The operator confirmed all seven as
correct on 2026-09-02, and five have since been exercised against the live
API. Treat them as verified.

Hardsell.name: Hard Sell (Night)
Hardsell.note: base Hardsell is the night map

FragrantShore.name: Fragrant Shore (Day)
FragrantShore.note: base FragrantShore is the DAY map; user-confirmed 2026-09-02

LVL_FragrantShore.name: Fragrant Shore (Day)
LVL_FragrantShore.note: file-name fallback for reports predating map_short_name

LVL_Soundeclipse.name: Sound Eclipse
LVL_Soundeclipse.note: file-name fallback for reports predating map_short_name

LVL_Silverreef.name: Silver Reef
LVL_Silverreef.note: file-name fallback for reports predating map_short_name

se.name: Sound Eclipse
se.note: mapCode is safe here - Sound Eclipse has no Day/Night variant

sr.name: Silver Reef
sr.note: mapCode is safe here - Silver Reef has no Day/Night variant

ds.name: Diamond Spire
ds.note: mapCode is safe here - Diamond Spire has no Day/Night variant. The code itself was inferred from the sr/se/fs pattern rather than observed; it is only a fallback for reports predating map_short_name, so a wrong guess costs a refusal, not a mis-file
